newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, JUNE 2 - SUNDAY, JUNE 8.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, JUNE 2 - SUNDAY, JUNE 8.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
LUXEMBOURG - EU foreign ministers meet (Mon-Tues); main discussions focus on preparations for June 16-17 Amsterdam summit.
BRUSSELS - European Commission regular meeting (Weds).
LUXEMBOURG - EU health ministers meet (Thurs); main discussions focus on tobacco restrictions, blood and human tissues safety.

LUXEMBOURG - EU development ministers meet (Thurs); main discussions focus on future relations between the European Union and African, Caribbean and Pacific countries, support for indigenous peoples and co-financing of non-governmental organisations.
MONDAY, JUNE 2

LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU foreign ministers meet (0930/0830 GMT) (and Tues). Agenda includes preparation for June 16-17 Amsterdam EU summit, humane trapping standards, Observatory against Racism and Xenophobia, preparations for EU-Japan summit, future relations with Hong Kong, mid-term revision of decision on associated countries and overseas countries, former Yugoslavia, relations with Albania, relations with Great Lakes regions, Middle East peace process.
- (1630/1430 GMT) Ministers hold inter-governmental conference meeting on EU treaty reforms.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Conservatives in the European Parliament hold conference on "The common agricultural policy: politics, policies and pressures" (0915/0715 GMT). Speakers include: European Commissioner Fischler, Dutch Agriculture Minister Jozias van Aarsten, European Parliament deputies Olsson, Cunha, Plumb, Sturdy. Venue: EP, Belliard 62. Contact: Conservatives Secretariat (322) 284 5294.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Belgian Nuclear Society (BNS) holds conference on "Worldwide energy perspective and role of nuclear energy" (0930/0730 GMT) (and Tues). Venue: SAS Radisson Hotel. Contact: Serge Vanderperre (322) 773 9422.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Union's tobacco sector and consultants Pieda Plc hold n/conf to present a major pan-European study on the economic importance of the tobacco sector in the EU (1100/0900 GMT). Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: CECCM (322) 231 1797.
TUESDAY, JUNE 3
LUXEMBOURG (NEW ITEM) - EU foreign ministers continue inter-governmental conference meeting on EU treaty reforms.
FRANKFURT (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner de Silguy attends European Monetary Institute Council.
BRUSSELS - Bulgarian Prime Minister Ivan Kostov and Foreign Minister Nadegda Mihailova meet European Parliament president Jose Maria Gil-Robles (1000/0800 GMT).

BRUSSELS - The European Institute of Business Administration holds n/conf on "The competitiveness of European industry" (1700/1500 GMT). Venue: Hotel Royal Windsor. Contact: Helle Jensen (33) 1 60 72 4404.

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) holds conference on "For a Europe of civil and social rights" (and Weds). Speakers include: European Commission President Santer. Venue: European Parliament, Leopold Building room 3C50. Contact: ETUC (322) 224 0411.

BRUSSELS - CEO Summit Conference on Converging Technologies (and Weds). Speakers include: European Commissioners Van Miert and Bonino, Ameritech International President Walter Catlow, Microsoft Europe President Bernard Vergnes, DHL International Chairman Patrick Lupo. Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: (1) 216 479 8420.
WEDNESDAY, JUNE 4
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Commission regular meeting.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Commissioner Brittan on the harmonisation of insurance credits.
- Commissioner Papoutsis on associations and foundations.
- Commissioner Flynn on worker information and consultation in national companies.
- Commissioners Flynn, Wulf-Mathies, Fischler on the report on implementation of territorial employment pacts.
- Commissioners Liikanen and Gradin on mid-term report on budget management.
- Commissioner Bjerregaard on "auto oil" programe; and on genetically modified maize imports.
- Action plan for the internal market.
- Establishment of a scientific managing committee.
THURSDAY, JUNE 5

LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU health ministers meet (1000/0800 GMT). Agenda includes EU health monitoring and epidemiological surveillance network, doctors' movements in the EU, health aspects of drug use; blood safety and quality; fight against tobacco consumption; future actions in public health; promotion of public health; safety of medical devices; report on women's health in the European Community.

LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU development ministers meet (1000/0800 GMT). Agenda includes future EU relations with African, Caribbean and Pacific countries; support for indigenous peoples, coherence of EU development cooperation with its other policies, operational coordination in development cooperation between the EU and the member states, research and technological development in relation to the EU's development cooperation policy, financing of non-governmental organisations, follow-up to the Social Summit, (over lunch) United Nations General Assembly Special Session.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Community Shipowners' Associations (ECSA) holds n/conf on "Upwards of 50,000 jobs to go as a direct result of abolition of duty and tax free sales in EU ferry industry" (1100/0900 GMT). Venue: International Press Centre. Contact: Tim Marking, ECSA (322) 511 3940.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "Austria's first two and a half years of EU membership" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is: Permanent representative of Austria to the EU Manfred Schreich. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

BRUSSELS - European Mortgage Federation Chairman Alberto Costantini holds news conference on the occasion of the publication of the 1996 annual report (1100/0900 GMT). Venue: European Mortgage Federation, 14 avenue de la Joyeuse Entree. Contact: Nicole Dewindt (322) 285 4042.
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts K4 Committee (consisting of officials from interior ministeries of EU member states) meeting (and Fri). No agenda available yet.
FRIDAY, JUNE 6
THE HAGUE (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer and European Commissioner Flynn attend mini summit with employer and labour groups on "The social dialogue".

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - International Movement ATD Fourth World holds its fifth session of the Fourth World People's University to discuss poverty in Europe. Speakers include Economic and Social Committee President Tom Jenkins, European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles and European Commissioner Oreja. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - The Greek cultural association "Kyklos" holds discussion panel on "Greek-Turkish relations in a European perspective" (1930/1730 GMT). Venue: European Parliament, Belliard 53.
SATURDAY, JUNE 7
No events scheduled.
SUNDAY, JUNE 8
NOORDWIJK, The Netherlands - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Regional planning and regional policy" (To June 10).
